newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA FINANCE DEPT REJECTS FISCAL DEFICIT REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA FINANCE DEPT REJECTS FISCAL DEFICIT REPORT.

text.p: The department of finance on Wednesday disputed a report issued earlier in the day that South Africa's fiscal deficit was far worse than generally thought.
The report, by Cape Town-based BOE Asset Management, said this was the case because headline measurements of the size of public sector borrowing excluded key components of state spending.
However, the department said the calculations used in the article were incorrect.
"The Department of Finance is aware of the ideas expressed ...in the article released today. These ideas are not new," it said in a statement.
It said that the director-general of finance, Maria Ramos, had written to BOE about the article, highlighting the fact that its calculations were wrong.

Ramos' letter said that in keeping with the "cash" basis of the fiscal accounts, the extraordinary transfers through which the Reserve Bank had from time to time been recompensed for forward cover losses were -- contrary to the report's assertions -- reflected in the published accounts.
The report adopted a basis for calculation which exaggerated the deficit by an amount nearly twice as large as the adjustment required, it said.

"(The report) chooses to neglect the main source of acknowleged distortion in the conventional deficit, which is the absence of any adjustment for the effects of inflation. The required adjustment would of course be large in South Africa's case and would impact favourably on the deficit," Ramos said.

She added that the proper conclusion to draw from current trends and policy was that the fiscal challenge was being prudently addressed, and not that "a severe economic and financial crisis was inexorably building up".
